title: Dirty Frag CISO Dashboard

risk_posture.executive_summary: Dirty Frag is a post-compromise Linux local privilege-escalation risk that can expand a low-privileged foothold into root access on vulnerable systems. CISO priorities are kernel patch/reboot validation, local-access reduction, safe module exposure reduction, and post-compromise detection coverage.

kri_cards.name: Patch and reboot compliance
kri_cards.target: >= 95% prioritized Linux assets booted into remediated kernels

kri_cards.name: High-value hosts with unknown posture
kri_cards.target: 0 internet-facing or crown-jewel Linux hosts with unknown kernel posture

kri_cards.name: Relevant modules loaded without exception
kri_cards.target: 0 unauthorized esp4, esp6, or rxrpc exposures

kri_cards.name: Detection telemetry coverage
kri_cards.target: >= 90% prioritized hosts reporting process, file, auth, module, and kernel inventory telemetry

kri_cards.name: Suspicious escalation investigations
kri_cards.target: All staging-to-root-transition alerts triaged within incident SLA

priority_asset_segments.business_risk: Compromised SSH or web-shell access can escalate to root and expose customer-facing services.
priority_asset_segments.required_action: Patch and reboot first; verify shell-access controls and detection coverage.

priority_asset_segments.business_risk: A container foothold can become host-level risk if local execution reaches the node kernel.
priority_asset_segments.required_action: Validate node kernel posture, privileged container controls, host namespace restrictions, and runtime telemetry.

priority_asset_segments.business_risk: Affected modules may be operationally required, extending exposure until patched.
priority_asset_segments.required_action: Coordinate maintenance windows, document exceptions, and increase monitoring.

priority_asset_segments.business_risk: Observed post-compromise behaviors included application and session tampering patterns.
priority_asset_segments.required_action: Enable file/session monitoring and validate application integrity after suspected escalation.

priority_asset_segments.business_risk: Untrusted build workloads can create local execution opportunities on Linux hosts.
priority_asset_segments.required_action: Restrict runner privileges, isolate workloads, and verify rapid patch cadence.

workstreams.name: Patch and reboot
workstreams.success_measure: Prioritized Linux systems are booted into vendor-remediated kernels.

workstreams.name: Module exposure review
workstreams.success_measure: Unused esp4, esp6, and rxrpc exposure is blocked or has approved business exceptions.

workstreams.name: Threat hunting deployment
workstreams.success_measure: KQL, Sigma, and osquery hunts are deployed or mapped to equivalent telemetry.

workstreams.name: Linux access hardening
workstreams.success_measure: Unnecessary SSH, shell, service-account, and automation access paths are reduced.

workstreams.name: Exception governance
workstreams.success_measure: All delayed patching or module-disablement exceptions are time-bound and owner-approved.

decision_gates.condition: Internet-facing or high-value Linux host has vulnerable or unknown kernel posture
decision_gates.decision: Patch and reboot immediately; apply enhanced monitoring until validated.

decision_gates.condition: Host requires IPsec, VPN, or RxRPC and cannot disable modules
decision_gates.decision: Approve temporary exception only with compensating access controls, monitoring, and committed remediation date.

decision_gates.condition: Suspicious local staging followed by root transition is observed
decision_gates.decision: Treat as possible compromise; preserve evidence, isolate as appropriate, and run incident response.

decision_gates.condition: Confirmed exploitation or strong indicators exist
decision_gates.decision: Treat as full host compromise and validate application integrity, credentials, persistence, and downstream access.

data_sources: Linux auth logs and SSH session records
Module exposure checks from dirtyfrag_poc.py or osquery
